kept.text: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) explicitly exempts auto-replenishment of NETC FASTag and RuPay NCMC from the requirement to send a Pre-Debit Notification (PDN) at least 24 hours prior to debit.
While pre-transaction notification is generally required for e-mandates, the specific exception applies only to auto-replenishment balances of FASTag and NCMC.

flagged.text: Under this exemption, issuers are permitted to omit the advance notice message after a debit occurs for auto-replenishment transactions without violating RBI rules.
review_reasons: The cited notification rule concerns a different event phase. A pre-transaction exemption does not establish a post-transaction exemption, or vice versa.

reasons: The local model accepted the selected evidence as support.

quotes.quote: ## 6. Pre-transaction Notification (a) An issuer shall send a pre-transaction notification to the customer, at least 24 hours prior to the actual charge / debit. (b) The pre-transaction notification shall, at the minimum, inform the customer about the merchant’s name, transaction amount, date / time of debit, reference number of e-mandate, reason for debit, i.e., e-mandate registered by the customer. (c) The issuer shall provider a customer with a facility to opt-out of any particular transaction or the e-mandate. Any such opt-out shall be validated by the issuer using AFA. An intimation to this effect shall be sent to the customer. (d) Pre-transaction notification is not required for e-mandates registered to auto-replenish balances of FASTag, and National Common Mobility Card (NCMC).

original.text: Under this exemption, issuers are permitted to omit the advance notice message after a debit occurs for auto-replenishment transactions without violating RBI rules.
review_reasons: The cited notification rule concerns a different event phase. A pre-transaction exemption does not establish a post-transaction exemption, or vice versa.

candidate.text: Issuers are permitted to omit the pre-debit notification for auto-replenishment transactions under Circular RBI/2024-25/64 (Circular No. 207), but this exemption applies only to notifications sent before the debit occurs and does not authorize omitting any post-debit intimation messages.

reasons: The cited notification rule concerns a different event phase. A pre-transaction exemption does not establish a post-transaction exemption, or vice versa.
